text: 🔥🇲🇽 "We only stated facts. I stand by what I said, because I have proof of everything I say." "Which Morenista has been covered up? Let him say it." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 6, 2026 The new Somos party announced a lawsuit for moral damages and defamation against Sheinbaum and the Anti-Corruption Secretary after Thursday's report linking the Hernández Casillas electoral contractors to one of its members. Former INE head Lorenzo Córdova said he backs auditing every contract but hoped no Morenista would be covered up. Sheinbaum replied that several Morena municipal presidents have been arrested for links to criminal groups or corruption. On the INE's 37-billion-peso 2027 budget, which the Chamber of Deputies plans to cut by 5 billion: "Yes, because it was an inflated budget."

🇲🇽🎨 "That cultural wealth doesn't exist anywhere else in the world, and it is a source of pride for all of us." "For many years in our country, and it still happens, if a person speaks an Indigenous language, they are discriminated against." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 6, 2026 Voces Vivas, the community culture festival, fills Mexico City's Zócalo on Saturday, Nov 7, from 5:30 p.m.: more than 1,000 children from 28 states and 181 municipalities perform, in 17 languages, the Cora, Wixárika, Chatino and Zoque Popoluca story of the opossum who stole fire for humanity. Canal 22 airs it live. From Nov 12 to 15, the Original textile and folk art fair returns to Los Pinos with 580 master artisans and about 174,000 pieces. The artisans sell about 93% of what they bring, with no middlemen, and the network has grown to almost 13,000 artisans in two years.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Mexico City Congress Opens Debate on Dignified Death and Fair Rents</u>

On November 4, Mexico City's Congress approved agreements to hold public forums on two fronts: the right to a dignified death (euthanasia) and Clara Brugada's Fair, Reasonable and Affordable Rents law, which would register every lease on a digital platform run by the city's ADIP.

Specialists, academics and collectives get their say before anything goes to a vote.
banner: CDMX: FORUMS ON EUTHANASIA & FAIR RENTS

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>Edomex Closes In on $20 Billion in Foreign Investment</u>

Mexico State is nearing US$20 billion in foreign direct investment, El Economista reports, and economic development secretary Laura Teresa González Hernández expects to hold the pace through the final quarter.

What's in the pipeline: logistics, light manufacturing, pharma, aerospace, electromobility and several data centers in negotiation. Four specialized universities are planned for 2027–2028 to train the workforce.

🇲🇽☀️ <u>From Chiapas to Palacio Nacional: Xóchitl's Solar Heater Gets State Backing</u>

Sheinbaum announced that SEP, SECIHTI and SENER will refine and promote "Baño Calientito," the solar water heater built by Xóchitl Guadalupe Cruz López, 17, from San Cristóbal de las Casas. She started it at age 8 with black-painted PET bottles, hoses, wood and reused glass.

They met for 20 minutes at Palacio Nacional on November 5. On November 10, Xóchitl returns with other young Mexicans who have won international awards in math and science.
banner: CHIAPAS TEEN'S SOLAR HEATER GETS STATE BACKING

🇲🇽💉 <u>UNAM Opens a Free Mega Vaccination Center: 100,000 Doses</u>

From November 9 to 13, UNAM's Olympic Stadium becomes a free vaccination hub open to the general public, not just students: 100,000 doses, 25,000 each against COVID, influenza, measles and pneumococcus, supplied by federal Health, Mexico City, IMSS and ISSSTE.

UNAM health director Gustavo Olaiz points to measles, which still shows high incidence across the country.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>Mexico City Closes Ranks With Cuba: "A Project of Asphyxiation"</u>

At INAH's National Museum of World Cultures in Mexico City, Cuban diplomats, solidarity organizers and artists gathered for "Cuba Today: Challenges, Solidarity and Action" to call for closing ranks with the island against Washington's squeeze.

Johana Tablada of the Cuban embassy: "We are being subjected to pressure like no other nation." Former culture minister Abel Prieto said calling it a blockade "falls short." It is "a project of asphyxiation."
banner: CUBA: CDMX CLOSES RANKS VS. US SQUEEZE

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum on Paraguay: "Separate Economic Power From Political Power"</u>

Asked about Paraguayan president Santiago Peña, now facing impeachment after Ueno Bank, a bank tied to a group he held shares in until March 2025, collapsed and froze the accounts of some 3 million people, Sheinbaum restated the line her movement has held for decades: "We have always said there must be a separation between economic power and political power. Each to its own part."

Her shorthand for Mexico's neoliberal era: "It was 36 years of total linkage."

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE: 87% of Its New Renewable Capacity Comes Through State-Majority Partnerships</u>

CFE director Emilia Calleja reported that 87.3% of the utility's planned renewable expansion is in mixed projects: 38 projects totaling 8,026 MW of generation plus more than 2,500 MW of storage, with an estimated investment of 204.5 billion pesos ($10.6 billion), El Economista reports.

The model: CFE makes the project bankable, the private partner finances it, the state keeps 54% ownership, and CFE buys 70% of the power. "The recovery of CFE's public character does not mean closing the door to private participation," Calleja said.

Private capital comes in. The state keeps control.
banner: CFE: 87% OF NEW RENEWABLES STATE-LED MIXED

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Maru Campos Drops a Taddei Ally From Chihuahua's Security Cabinet</u>

Claudia Arlett Espino, a former INE official known as one of Guadalupe Taddei's closest associates, is out of Chihuahua's Public Security Secretariat, effective November 30. She had joined PAN governor Maru Campos's government just one month after leaving the INE.

Espino sat in meetings and negotiations with the electoral suppliers now under investigation. It was PAN national president Jorge Romero who had to ask Campos to review the hire. The opposition calls Taddei a Morena creature; her inner circle landed a job in a PAN cabinet.
banner: CHIHUAHUA: TADDEI ALLY OUT OF PAN CABINET
